newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: CA says buyer likely an existing suitor.
newsitem.headline: CA says buyer likely an existing suitor.

text.p: Creditanstalt-Bankverein chief executive Guido Schmidt-Chiari on Tuesday said the buyer for the government's majority stake in the bank would likely come from the present group of suitors.
"I can tell you, the buyer won't come out of the blue," he said. "It's consistent with the interests of Creditanstalt's shareholders, that the bank joins forces with an Italian and a German group."

On Monday, Finance Minister Viktor Klima, in charge of the sale of the state's 70 percent voting stake in Austria's flagship bank, turned down the only firm bid from an Austro-Italian-German group around insurer EA Generali.
Klima said the bid from the consortium, which also includes Germany's Commerzbank and Banca Commerciale Italiana, fell short of the three main conditions laid down by the government in October 1995.
The government insists on selling its entire stake of around 19.9 million shares, ensuring the protection of national interests and guaranteeing "the best possible price" for the stake, Klima said.

Klima, desperate to use the proceeds from the sale to fill the state's bare coffers, said Creditanstalt would now work with the state's advisor J.P. Morgan to update the memorandum the U.S. investment house prepared last year and come up with a new procedure for privatisation within a few weeks.
Schmidt-Chiari, speaking at the Club of Economic Journalists, declined to comment on how the bid would be updated. "That's up to the owner (Klima)."

But Schmidt-Chiari added that while the bank had no ideal partner in mind, it was above all of "the utmost importance that we work together with a German financial institution." -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12 274
